questions.q: In a ratio a : b, we read it as 'for every a units of the first quantity there are ___ of the second quantity'. Which fills the blank?
questions.a: b units

questions.q:
Match each ratio in Column I with its simplest form in Column II.
Column I: I. 18 : 12  II. 8 : 12  III. 20 : 25  IV. 25 : 20
Column II: A. 2 : 3  B. 5 : 4  C. 3 : 2  D. 4 : 5
questions.a: I-C, II-A, III-D, IV-B

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The ratio 9 : 15 is not in its simplest form.
Reason (R): 9 and 15 have the common factor 3, so both terms can be divided by 3.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: Write the ratio 48 : 36 in its simplest form. (a) Find the HCF of 48 and 36. (b) Divide both terms by it.
questions.a: (a) The HCF of 48 and 36 is 12. (b) 48 / 12 = 4 and 36 / 12 = 3, so the simplest form is 4 : 3.
s: Divides both terms by 12 to get 4 : 3

questions.q: A class has 40 students, and 24 of them are girls. (a) How many boys are there? (b) Write the ratio of boys to girls. (c) Write this ratio in its simplest form.
questions.a: (a) 40 - 24 = 16 boys. (b) The ratio of boys to girls is 16 : 24. (c) The HCF of 16 and 24 is 8, so the simplest form is 2 : 3.
s: (c) Divides by the HCF 8 to get 2 : 3

questions.q: Four ratios are reduced to their simplest forms. Which one of them does NOT give the same simplest form as the other three?
The simplest form of a ratio is 5 : 6. Anil says the original numbers could be 35 and 42. Bela says they could be 45 and 54. (a) Check Anil's pair. (b) Check Bela's pair. (c) Who is right?
questions.a: (a) 35 : 42, with HCF 7, gives 5 : 6, so Anil's pair works. (b) 45 : 54, with HCF 9, gives 5 : 6, so Bela's pair works. (c) Both are right: many different pairs reduce to the same simplest form.
s: (c) Concludes both are right because different pairs can share one simplest form

questions.q: True or False: Dividing both terms of 24 : 36 by 4 gives 6 : 9, which is therefore the simplest form of 24 : 36. Give a reason.
questions.a: False. 6 : 9 can be reduced further, because 6 and 9 still have the common factor 3. The HCF of 24 and 36 is 12, so the simplest form is 2 : 3.
s: Reasons that 6 and 9 share the factor 3 and the HCF is 12, giving 2 : 3

questions.q:
A school librarian keeps story books and science books on three shelves. Shelf A has 48 story books and 36 science books. Shelf B has 40 story books and 24 science books. Shelf C has 30 story books and 18 science books. She wants every shelf to have the same ratio of story books to science books as Shelf A, without moving any story books.
(a) Write the ratio of story books to science books on each shelf in its simplest form.
(b) Which two shelves have proportional ratios? Are they proportional to Shelf A?
(c) How many science books should be added to Shelf B so that its ratio matches Shelf A?
(d) A helper says, 'Shelves B and C have the same ratio, so adding the same number of science books to Shelf C will make it match Shelf A too.' Is the helper right? Check and justify.
questions.a: (a) Shelf A: 48 : 36 = 4 : 3. Shelf B: 40 : 24 = 5 : 3. Shelf C: 30 : 18 = 5 : 3. (b) Shelves B and C are proportional to each other (both 5 : 3), but neither is proportional to Shelf A, because 5 : 3 is not 4 : 3. (c) 4 : 3 :: 40 : x gives 4x = 120, so x = 30 science books; Shelf B has 24, so 6 must be added. (d) No. Adding 6 to Shelf C gives 30 : 24 = 5 : 4, not 4 : 3; adding the same number to both shelves does not keep a proportion. Shelf C would need 4 : 3 :: 30 : y, so y = 22.5, which is not a whole number, so adding science books alone can never make Shelf C match.
s: (b) Names B and C as proportional to each other and not to A
(c) Finds 30 science books needed, so 6 to be added to Shelf B
(d) Shows Shelf C becomes 5 : 4 (or needs 22.5 books) and says the helper is wrong

questions.q: A school poster is 90 cm wide and 60 cm high. A print shop offers three other sizes: P is 45 cm by 30 cm, Q is 75 cm by 45 cm and R is 120 cm by 80 cm (width by height). (a) Which of P, Q and R have the same shape as the poster? Use simplest forms. (b) Rohan says, 'Q is 15 cm narrower and 15 cm shorter than the poster, so it has the same shape.' Explain his mistake. (c) The notice board has a space 84 cm wide and 60 cm high. Find the largest copy of the poster's shape that fits in this space.
questions.a: (a) The poster is 90 : 60 = 3 : 2. P is 45 : 30 = 3 : 2 and R is 120 : 80 = 3 : 2, so P and R have the same shape; Q is 75 : 45 = 5 : 3, so it does not. (b) Taking away the same length from both sides is a change by subtraction, not by the same multiplying factor, so the ratio changes from 3 : 2 to 5 : 3 and Q looks distorted. (c) If the copy is 84 cm wide, 3 : 2 :: 84 : h gives h = 56 cm, which fits in 60 cm. If it is 60 cm high, the width would be 90 cm, which is more than 84 cm. So the largest copy is 84 cm wide and 56 cm high.
s: (a) Finds 3 : 2 for the poster, P and R, 5 : 3 for Q, and names P and R
(b) Says subtracting the same amount is not the same factor, so the ratio changes to 5 : 3
(c) Tests both sides and finds the copy 84 cm by 56 cm

questions.q: Which of the following is a true statement of proportion?
Find the missing term in the proportion 5 : 8 :: 15 : ___ .
Are the ratios 5 : 9 and 40 : 72 proportional? (a) Write 40 : 72 in its simplest form. (b) State your conclusion.
questions.a: (a) The HCF of 40 and 72 is 8, so 40 : 72 reduces to 5 : 9. (b) Both ratios have the same simplest form 5 : 9, so they are proportional.
s: (b) Concludes they are proportional because the simplest forms are equal

questions.q: True or False: 6 : 9 :: 10 : 15. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. In simplest form 6 : 9 is 2 : 3 and 10 : 15 is also 2 : 3, so the two ratios are proportional.

questions.q: The numbers of boys and girls in three classes are: Class 8A has 18 boys and 12 girls; Class 8B has 21 boys and 14 girls; Class 8C has 15 boys and 12 girls. (a) Write the ratio of boys to girls in 8A and in 8B in simplest form. (b) Write the ratio for 8C in simplest form. (c) Which classes have proportional ratios? (d) Class 8D has 24 boys and its ratio is proportional to that of 8A. How many girls does it have? (e) Class 8E has 36 girls and its ratio is proportional to that of 8A. How many boys does it have?
questions.a: (a) 18 : 12 = 3 : 2 and 21 : 14 = 3 : 2. (b) 15 : 12 = 5 : 4. (c) 8A and 8B are proportional (both 3 : 2); 8C is not. (d) 3 : 2 :: 24 : g gives g = 16 girls. (e) 3 : 2 :: b : 36 gives b = 54 boys.
s: (c) Names 8A and 8B as proportional and 8C as not

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. A 15 cm by 10 cm photo and a 9 cm by 6 cm photo have proportional width-to-height ratios.
II. A 12 cm by 8 cm photo and an 18 cm by 14 cm photo have proportional width-to-height ratios.
III. 20 : 25 :: 4 : 5.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: I and III only

questions.q: A painter mixes 12 mL of white paint with 20 mL of blue paint to get one shade of sky blue, and wants the same shade in other quantities. (a) How much blue paint goes with 3 mL of white paint? (b) How much white paint goes with 50 mL of blue paint? (c) How much blue paint goes with 21 mL of white paint?
questions.a: The ratio white : blue is 12 : 20, which is 3 : 5. (a) 3 mL of white needs 5 mL of blue. (b) 50 mL of blue needs 30 mL of white. (c) 12 : 20 :: 21 : b gives b = 35 mL of blue.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Adding 3 to both terms of 7 : 9 gives 10 : 12, and the ratios 7 : 9 and 10 : 12 are not proportional.
Reason (R): 7 : 9 is already in its simplest form, while 10 : 12 in its simplest form is 5 : 6, so the two ratios have different simplest forms.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q:
A designer has a school logo that is 45 mm wide and 30 mm high. A printer offers four sizes, written as width by height: Badge 30 mm by 20 mm, Sticker 60 mm by 45 mm, Banner 90 mm by 60 mm and Card 24 mm by 18 mm. The designer wants every printed copy to look exactly like the logo, with no stretching.
(a) Write the ratio of width to height of the logo in simplest form.
(b) Which of the four sizes keep the shape of the logo?
(c) The Sticker is to keep a width of 60 mm. What height would keep the shape?
(d) A poster copy is to be 210 mm wide. What height keeps the shape?
questions.a: (a) 45 : 30 has HCF 15, so it is 3 : 2. (b) Badge 30 : 20 is 3 : 2 and Banner 90 : 60 is 3 : 2, so these two keep the shape; Sticker 60 : 45 is 4 : 3 and Card 24 : 18 is 4 : 3, so they do not. (c) 3 : 2 :: 60 : h gives h = 40 mm. (d) 3 : 2 :: 210 : h gives h = 140 mm.
s: (b) Names Badge and Banner, with 4 : 3 for the other two

questions.q:
In a school sports day, Red House has 72 points and Blue House has 48 points. After one more event, each house gains 8 points, so Red House has 80 and Blue House has 56. Raj says, 'Both houses gained the same points, so the ratio of their scores is still the same.'
(a) Write the ratio of Red's score to Blue's score before the event, in simplest form.
(b) Write the ratio after the event, in simplest form.
(c) Is Raj right? Give a reason.
(d) Show a change of both scores that would keep the ratio the same.
questions.a: (a) 72 : 48 = 3 : 2. (b) 80 : 56 = 10 : 7. (c) Raj is wrong: 3 : 2 and 10 : 7 are different, so the ratios are not proportional; adding the same number to both terms changes the ratio. (d) Multiplying both scores by the same factor keeps it, for example doubling gives 144 : 96, which is 3 : 2.
s: (c) Says Raj is wrong because 3 : 2 and 10 : 7 differ, adding the same number changes the ratio
(d) Gives a same-factor change such as 144 : 96 that keeps 3 : 2

questions.q:
In Aryabhata's Rule of Three, pramana : phala :: ichchha : ichchhaphala. Match each term in Column I with its meaning in Column II.
Column I: I. pramana  II. phala  III. ichchha  IV. ichchhaphala
Column II: A. yield  B. measure  C. requisition  D. fruit
questions.a: I-B, II-D, III-C, IV-A

questions.q: If a : b :: c : d, which of the following is always true?
questions.a: a x d = b x c
o: a x d = b x c
a x b = c x d
a x c = b x d

questions.q: In a Rule of Three problem, the pramana is 15 m of cloth, the phala is Rs 240 and the ichchha is 9 m of cloth. (a) Write the proportion in the form pramana : phala :: ichchha : ichchhaphala. (b) Find the ichchhaphala.
questions.a: (a) 15 : 240 :: 9 : ichchhaphala. (b) Ichchhaphala = (240 x 9) / 15 = Rs 144.

questions.q: 8 pencils cost Rs 36 at a shop. The cost of 20 pencils at the same rate is to be found. (a) Write the proportion for the cost x of 20 pencils. (b) Use cross multiplication on it. (c) Find x.
True or False: If 3 : 5 :: 9 : 15, then 3 x 9 = 5 x 15. Give a reason.
questions.a: False. Cross multiplication says a x d = b x c, so 3 x 15 = 5 x 9 (both 45). The products 3 x 9 = 27 and 5 x 15 = 75 are not equal.
s: Reasons with the cross products 3 x 15 = 5 x 9 = 45, while 27 and 75 differ

questions.q: Use cross multiplication to solve the proportion 8 : 14 :: 28 : x. What is x?
Tara walks 3/4 km in 10 minutes and keeps the same pace. She wants to know how long she takes to walk 3 km. (a) Write the proportion with t minutes for 3 km. (b) Use cross multiplication. (c) Find t.
s: (b) Cross multiplies to get (3/4) x t = 30

questions.q: Ravi says, 'If a : b :: c : d, then a + d = b + c.' Test his claim on the proportion 2 : 3 :: 4 : 6. (a) Show that 2 : 3 :: 4 : 6 is true. (b) Find a + d and b + c. (c) Find a x d and b x c, and say who is right about the rule.
questions.a: (a) 4 : 6 reduces to 2 : 3, so 2 : 3 :: 4 : 6 is true. (b) a + d = 2 + 6 = 8 but b + c = 3 + 4 = 7, so Ravi's rule fails. (c) a x d = 12 and b x c = 12 are equal, so the correct rule is cross multiplication, ad = bc.
s: (b) Finds 8 and 7, so Ravi's sum rule fails
(c) Finds 12 and 12 and states the rule ad = bc

questions.q:
A tap fills 240 litres of water in 15 minutes at a steady rate. A farmer needs 1,000 litres for his cattle trough, but the water supply will be on for only 62 minutes.
(a) Form a proportion and find the time the tap needs to give 1,000 litres.
(b) Is 62 minutes enough? Say why.
(c) How many litres will the tap give in 62 minutes?
(d) By how many litres will the farmer fall short?
questions.a: (a) 240 : 15 :: 1,000 : t, so t = 15 x 1,000 / 240 = 62.5 minutes. (b) No, because 62.5 minutes are needed and only 62 are available. (c) 240 : 15 :: L : 62, so L = 240 x 62 / 15 = 992 litres. (d) 1,000 - 992 = 8 litres short.
s: (a) Sets up the proportion and finds 62.5 minutes
(b) Says 62 minutes is not enough since 62.5 are needed

questions.q: A painter paints 2 1/4 m of a fence in 3/4 of an hour. At the same rate, how many metres of fence does she paint in 6 hours? (a) Name the pramana, phala and ichchha in this problem. (b) Set up the proportion. (c) Find the ichchhaphala.
questions.a: (a) The pramana is 3/4 hour (the measure), the phala is 9/4 m (the fruit) and the ichchha is 6 hours (the requisition). (b) 3/4 : 9/4 :: 6 : x. (c) x = (9/4 x 6) / (3/4) = (54/4) x (4/3) = 18 m.
s: (a) Names pramana 3/4 hour, phala 9/4 m and ichchha 6 hours

questions.q: A bus travels 60 km in 90 minutes. To find the distance it covers in 3 hours at the same speed, Meena writes 90 : 60 :: 3 : ? . What must she do first?
questions.a: Write 3 hours as 180 minutes

questions.q: A car uses 6 litres of petrol to travel 90 km. At the same rate, how many litres does it need for 150 km?
questions.a: 10 litres

questions.q: A machine packs 30 packets in 40 seconds. (a) Write 2 minutes in seconds and write a proportion for x, the number of packets it packs in 2 minutes at the same rate. (b) Find x.
questions.a: (a) 2 minutes = 120 seconds, so 40 : 30 :: 120 : x. (b) 40x = 30 x 120 = 3,600, so x = 90 packets.

questions.q: True or False: A cyclist rides 15 km in 1 hour at a steady speed, so the Rule of Three correctly gives 45 km as the distance covered in 3 hours. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. At a steady speed the distance changes by the same factor as the time, so 1 : 15 :: 3 : 45 holds. Time is multiplied by 3 and so is the distance.
s: Reasons that time and distance change by the same factor (1 : 15 :: 3 : 45)

questions.q: A tea stall uses 250 g of tea leaves to make 40 cups of tea. It wants to know how many cups it can make with a 2 kg pack of tea leaves at the same rate. (a) Write 2 kg in grams. (b) Write the proportion with c cups for the 2 kg pack. (c) Find c.
A train takes 3 hours to cover a journey at 60 km/h. Anita writes 60 : 3 :: 90 : ? to find the time at 90 km/h. Why is this wrong?
questions.a: Time decreases when speed increases, so the two are not in direct proportion
o: Time decreases when speed increases, so the two are not in direct proportion
Speed and time must be written in the same units
90 is larger than 60, so the ratio cannot be formed
The ratio 60 : 3 cannot be written in simplest form

questions.q: One shop sells 250 g of tea for Rs 150. Another shop sells 1 kg of the same tea for Rs 560. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: The 1 kg packet is cheaper, because 1 kg at the first shop's rate would cost Rs 600
o: The 1 kg packet is cheaper, because 1 kg at the first shop's rate would cost Rs 600
The 250 g packet is cheaper, because Rs 150 is less than Rs 560
Both are priced at the same rate per gram
The 250 g packet is cheaper, because 1 kg at its rate would cost Rs 500

questions.q: Asha is 110 cm tall at age 6 and 150 cm tall at age 12. Her cousin says, 'Height is proportional to age.' (a) Test whether 6 : 110 :: 12 : 150 is true by cross multiplication. (b) What height would the Rule of Three give at age 12? (c) State your conclusion.
questions.a: (a) 6 x 150 = 900 but 110 x 12 = 1,320; they are not equal, so 6 : 110 :: 12 : 150 is false. (b) The Rule of Three would give 110 x 12 / 6 = 220 cm, which is unrealistic. (c) Height is not proportional to age, so the Rule of Three cannot be used here.
s: (a) Finds the cross products 900 and 1,320 and says they differ
(b) Finds 220 cm and says it is unrealistic
(c) Concludes height is not proportional to age

questions.q:
A shop sells one bar of soap of 75 g for Rs 30. It also sells a pack of 4 such bars, of total weight 300 g, for Rs 100.
(a) Write the ratio of weight to price for the single bar in simplest form.
(b) Write the same ratio for the pack in simplest form.
(c) Are the two ratios proportional?
(d) If the price were proportional to the weight of the single bar, what would 300 g cost?
(e) Which is the better buy per 75 g, the single bar or the pack? Give the price per 75 g in the pack.
questions.a: (a) 75 : 30 = 5 : 2. (b) 300 : 100 = 3 : 1. (c) No, since 5 : 2 and 3 : 1 are different. (d) 75 : 30 :: 300 : p gives p = Rs 120. (e) The pack costs 100 / 4 = Rs 25 per 75 g, which is less than Rs 30, so the pack is the better buy.
s: (e) Finds Rs 25 per 75 g and says the pack is the better buy

questions.q: A school has 480 students and 12 water taps. Next year it will have 640 students. The principal wants the same students-to-taps ratio. (a) How many taps are needed for 640 students? (b) The school can afford only 14 taps. Check by cross multiplication whether 480 : 12 :: 640 : 14 is true. (c) With 14 taps, will each tap serve more students than now? Give the numbers.
questions.a: (a) 480 : 12 :: 640 : t gives t = 12 x 640 / 480 = 16 taps. (b) 480 x 14 = 6,720 and 12 x 640 = 7,680; they are not equal, so the ratios are not proportional. (c) Now each tap serves 480 / 12 = 40 students; with 14 taps each serves about 640 / 14 = 45.7 students, which is more.
s: (b) Finds 6,720 and 7,680 and says not proportional
(c) Compares 40 students per tap with about 45.7 and says more

questions.q: Rs 350 is divided between Tara and Uma in the ratio 3 : 4. What is Uma's share?
questions.a: Rs 200

questions.q: A quantity x is to be divided in the ratio m : n. What is the size of each equal group?
questions.a: x / (m + n)

questions.q:
Assertion (A): When 40 is divided in the ratio 3 : 5, the parts are 15 and 25.
Reason (R): There are 3 + 5 = 8 groups, each of size 40 / 8 = 5, and the parts are 3 groups and 5 groups.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: Rs 1,200 is shared between Mira and Neel in the ratio 1 : 5. (a) Find the value of one group. (b) Find each share.
questions.a: (a) There are 1 + 5 = 6 groups, so one group is 1,200 / 6 = Rs 200. (b) Mira gets 1 x 200 = Rs 200 and Neel gets 5 x 200 = Rs 1,000.

questions.q: Dev invested Rs 30,000 and Esha invested Rs 90,000 in a bakery. They earn a profit of Rs 6,000 and share it in the ratio of their investments. (a) Write the ratio of their investments in simplest form. (b) Find the value of one group. (c) Find each person's share.
questions.a: (a) 30,000 : 90,000 = 1 : 3. (b) There are 4 groups, so one group is 6,000 / 4 = Rs 1,500. (c) Dev gets Rs 1,500 and Esha gets 3 x 1,500 = Rs 4,500.

questions.q: A rope 84 cm long is cut into two pieces in the ratio 3 : 4. The longer piece is then cut into two pieces in the ratio 1 : 2. How long is the shortest of the three pieces?
questions.a: 16 cm

questions.q: A school has 450 students, and the ratio of boys to girls is 7 : 8. (a) How many girls are there? (b) How many more girls than boys are there?
questions.a: (a) There are 7 + 8 = 15 groups of 450 / 15 = 30, so girls = 8 x 30 = 240. (b) Boys = 7 x 30 = 210, so there are 240 - 210 = 30 more girls.

questions.q: Kiran says, 'To divide 84 in the ratio 3 : 4, I divide 84 by 3 and by 4 and get 28 and 21.' (a) Show that his parts do not add up to 84. (b) State the correct size of each group. (c) Find the correct parts.
questions.a: (a) 28 + 21 = 49, which is not 84, so the method is wrong. (b) The number of groups is 3 + 4 = 7, so each group is 84 / 7 = 12. (c) The parts are 3 x 12 = 36 and 4 x 12 = 48, which add up to 84.

questions.q:
A school canteen has 120 kg of flour made of wheat flour and ragi flour in the ratio 7 : 3. The cook adds 24 kg more ragi flour, but the nutrition teacher says the two flours should be in equal amounts, a ratio of 1 : 1, with the wheat flour left as it is.
(a) Find the amount of each flour in the original mixture.
(b) Find the amount of ragi flour after the 24 kg are added.
(c) Write the new ratio of wheat flour to ragi flour in simplest form.
(d) How much ragi flour must there be for the ratio to be 1 : 1?
(e) How much more ragi flour must still be added after the first 24 kg?
questions.a: (a) 7 + 3 = 10 groups of 12 kg, so wheat flour is 84 kg and ragi flour is 36 kg. (b) 36 + 24 = 60 kg of ragi flour. (c) 84 : 60 has HCF 12, so it is 7 : 5. (d) For a 1 : 1 ratio the ragi flour must equal the wheat flour, 84 kg. (e) 84 - 60 = 24 kg more must still be added.
s: (a) Finds 84 kg wheat flour and 36 kg ragi flour
(d) Says the ragi flour must be 84 kg

questions.q: Team A has 40 members and the ratio of boys to girls in it is 3 : 2. Team B has 45 members and its ratio of boys to girls is 4 : 5. (a) Find the number of boys and girls in Team A. (b) Find the number of boys and girls in Team B. (c) The two teams join. Write the new ratio of boys to girls in simplest form and say whether it equals 3 : 2 or 4 : 5.
questions.a: (a) Team A has 8 per group: 3 x 8 = 24 boys and 2 x 8 = 16 girls. (b) Team B has 5 per group: 4 x 5 = 20 boys and 5 x 5 = 25 girls. (c) Together there are 44 boys and 41 girls, so the ratio is 44 : 41, which is already in simplest form and equals neither 3 : 2 nor 4 : 5.
s: (a) Finds 24 boys and 16 girls in Team A
(b) Finds 20 boys and 25 girls in Team B
(c) Finds 44 : 41 and says it equals neither 3 : 2 nor 4 : 5

questions.q: How many square metres make 1 hectare?
questions.a: 10,000 square metres

questions.q: Using Fahrenheit = (9/5) x Celsius + 32, what is 10 degrees Celsius in degrees Fahrenheit?
questions.a: 50 degrees Fahrenheit

questions.q: A metal rod is 5 m long. Use 1 metre = 3.281 feet. (a) Write the multiplication that gives its length in feet. (b) Find the length in feet.
questions.a: (a) Length in feet = 5 x 3.281. (b) 5 x 3.281 = 16.405 feet.

questions.q: A fish tank holds 25 litres of water. Use 1 litre = 1,000 mL and 1 mL = 1 cc. (a) Write the capacity in mL. (b) Write the capacity in cc. (c) How many 500 mL bottles of water fill the tank?
questions.a: (a) 25 x 1,000 = 25,000 mL. (b) Since 1 mL = 1 cc, the tank holds 25,000 cc. (c) 25,000 / 500 = 50 bottles.

questions.q:
Use the conversion facts given in the chapter to convert each of the following, showing the working.
(a) 3 m into feet
(b) 3 acres into square feet
(c) 2 hectares into square metres
(d) 86 degrees Fahrenheit into degrees Celsius
questions.a: (a) 3 x 3.281 = 9.843 feet. (b) 3 x 43,560 = 1,30,680 square feet. (c) 2 x 10,000 = 20,000 square metres. (d) Celsius = (5/9) x (86 - 32) = (5/9) x 54 = 30 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: Which of these is the lowest temperature?
questions.a: 65 degrees Fahrenheit

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. 1 litre is equal to 1,000 cc.
II. A temperature of 50 degrees Celsius is 122 degrees Fahrenheit.
III. 1 hectare is equal to 100 square metres.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: I and II only

questions.q: A farmer's plot is 240 ft long and 363 ft wide. A fertiliser is advised at 25 kg for every acre (1 acre = 43,560 square feet). (a) Find the area of the plot in square feet. (b) Convert it to acres. (c) How much fertiliser does he need?
questions.a: (a) 240 x 363 = 87,120 square feet. (b) 87,120 / 43,560 = 2 acres. (c) 2 x 25 = 50 kg of fertiliser.

questions.q:
A school fair has a juice stall with one full 24-litre can of lemon juice. The stall can sell the juice in one of two ways. Plan 1: paper cups of 200 mL each, sold at Rs 15 a cup. Plan 2: bottles that hold 300 cc each, sold at Rs 20 a bottle. All the juice will be sold. Use 1 litre = 1,000 mL and 1 mL = 1 cc.
(a) Write the juice in the can in millilitres.
(b) How many cups can be filled under Plan 1, and how much money will they bring?
(c) How many bottles can be filled under Plan 2, and how much money will they bring?
(d) Which plan should the stall choose to earn more, and by how much?
s: (c) Uses 300 cc = 300 mL, finds 80 bottles and Rs 1,600
(d) Chooses Plan 1, which earns Rs 200 more

questions.q:
A school must hold an exam for 78 students and can book one of two halls for the day. Hall A has a floor area of 150 square metres and costs Rs 8,000. Hall B has a floor area of 1,500 square feet and costs Rs 5,000. Each student needs 20 square feet of floor space. Use 1 square metre = 10.764 square feet.
(a) Find the floor area of Hall A in square feet.
(b) Which hall is larger, and by how many square feet?
(c) How many students can each hall seat?
(d) Which hall should the school book? Justify your choice.
questions.a: (a) 150 x 10.764 = 1,614.6 square feet. (b) Hall A is larger by 1,614.6 - 1,500 = 114.6 square feet. (c) Hall A: 1,614.6 / 20 = 80.73, so 80 students. Hall B: 1,500 / 20 = 75 students. (d) Hall A. Hall B is cheaper, but it seats only 75, fewer than the 78 students, while Hall A seats 80.
s: (b) Says Hall A is larger by 114.6 square feet
(c) Finds 80 students for Hall A and 75 for Hall B
(d) Chooses Hall A because Hall B cannot seat 78
